newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's H1 net up 20 pct at $37.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's H1 net up 20 pct at $37.7 mln.

text.p: Morocco's ONA Group, one of the largest companies in Africa, said on Thursday it posted a consolidated net profit of $37.7 million in the first half of 1996, due mainly to agro-industry and mining sectors.

ONA, the biggest private company in Morocco with holdings in more than 100 firms, showed a 20.6 percent rise in its consolidated net profit to 328.6 million dirhams in the period of January-June 1996 compared with 272.4 million dirhams in the first half of 1995.
Detailed results were announced by ONA's president Fouad Filali following a meeting of the conglomerate's board of directors.
ONA's long term debt dropped to 1.62 billion dirhams in the first half of 1996, from 2.89 billion dirhams in the same period last year.
"These good results were achieved due mainly to the performance of agro-industry and mining sectors," Filali told reporters.
But the group's turnover dropped 2.5 percent to around 8.8 billion dirhams in the period of January-June 1996 compared with the same period last year.
The decline reflected Morocco's sluggish economic situation in the first half of 1996 and the priority given by ONA group to the improvement of its profitability, Filali said.
"The group will focus its activity in the future on the core business which are mining, finance, international and agro-industry sectors," he said.
With the undergoing liberalisation, the group plans to consolidate its market shares in the strategic agro-industry which is expected to face tough competition in the coming years.
ONA and its subsidiaries control between 65 and 80 percent of Morocco's edible oil, sugar and milk market, stockbrokers said.
One of the 46 listed companies on the Casablanca stock market, ONA was traded on Thursday at 495 dirhams per share, up 10 dirhams over the previous session.

The conglomerate's listed subsidiaries sugar refinery Cosumar, agro-industry Centrale Laitiere, edible oil firm Lesieur and Financiere Diwan, all together posted positive results in the first half of 1996 compared with the same period last year, the group said.
The group gave no forecast for the 1996/97 results but analysts at Casablanca Finance Intermediation expect ONA's consolidated net profit to reach an estimated 720 million dirhams by end 1996.
Established in 1919, ONA Group (former Omnium Nord Africain), has a market capitalisation of 8.1 billion dirhams.
ONA's president Fouad Filali, who is the son of Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali, is also the son-in-law of Morocco's King Hassan.
